 Comment React Share Heartbreak: Arthur Fils Retires Hurt Against Fritz in Basel
 The Frenchman was forced to retire in the Basel quarterfinals, just days before the Paris Masters 1000 begins.
 French player Arthur Fils reacts during his match against Monegasque Valentin Vacherot in the men's singles quarterfinals of the ATP Tour Japan Open Tennis Championships at Ariake Tennis Park in Tokyo on October 4, 2026. © RIE KIKUCHI / AFP Arthur Millot 30/10/2026, 16:36 1 min to read Follow us ATP 500 Bâle Fils It's another bitter disappointment for Arthur Fils.
 Facing Taylor Fritz in the quarterfinals of the ATP 500 in Basel, the French No. 1 retired in the second set, with the score at 6-2, 2-0 in his opponent's favor.
 Remove ads He had called a medical timeout at 5-2 in the first set for lower back pain and appeared to be struggling with his pushes and movement, before clearly conceding the opening set.
 A curse?
 It seems like a curse strikes whenever big French events loom.
 His last retirement came at the Rome Masters 1000, just days before the start of Roland-Garros.
 Indeed, the player is seeded at home, at the Paris Masters 1000, which begins next Monday.
 Whether he will be able to take his place in the French capital remains to be seen. Fingers crossed.
